newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: State prosecutors open South Africa oil industry probe.
newsitem.headline: State prosecutors open South Africa oil industry probe.

text.p: State prosecutors have opened a probe into South Africa's oil industry amid claims that the government was tricked into over-compensating oil producers by more than one billion rand ($208 million), according to a broadcast report.
Business Tonight television reported late on Tuesday that this was supposedly for lost market share caused by the expansion of fuels giant Sasol Ltd's synthetic fuel production in the 1980s.
It has been alleged that the oil companies overstated the loss suffered as a result of Sasol increasing its output in order to receive higher payments from the government.
State prosecutors in the Attorney-General's Office has already approached the industry for data on oil imports and exports since 1980.
No further details were immediately available.

Sasol on Monday posted a 21.7 percent jump in earnings to 393.1 cents a share in the year to June 25, in line with analysts' forecasts. Its synthetic fuels division posted a year operating profit up 47.7 percent to 1.51 billion rand.
